title: A Oath for the Garden
premise: The Guild of Small Mercies trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names that no longer fit—and Jonah Zhou, its youngest and last real member, keeps the ledgers that make the impossible accountable. When a child arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Jonah learns the child is the unbound half of King Aldric Vey, whose crown has been slowly wearing him instead of the reverse. To save both king and child, Jonah must break the guild's oldest law of invisibility, trading its hidden ledgers as leverage against the court sorcerer who forged the crown. In the end, Jonah chooses truth over the guild's survival: the guild dissolves into open light, the king is unbound at the cost of his throne, and the child—now whole—remembers Jonah's name in a language that means 'keeper.'
about_author: J. M. Eastwick is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging merchant guild records from coastal cities before turning to fiction. They write quiet fantasies about paperwork, power, and the people who keep accounts of miracles.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A tour of the dying guild through its ledgers: three aging members, a cellar of impossible inventory, and Jonah's careful bookkeeping keeping chaos legible. The emotional beat is tender melancholy—the comfort of routine on the edge of extinction.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On a night of first frost, a child arrives at the guild door speaking a language predating kingdoms; guildmaster Sefa recognizes it and goes pale. The child speaks Jonah's true name, which no ledger contains. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Refuse to Say
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with an interlude of the child's fragmented memories. Investigation reveals a sealed page in the founding ledger about a bargain struck with the first king—a crown made to hold something back. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything Jonah trusted.

chapters.title: The Crown That Wears the Man
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah and King Aldric, who dreams in the child's language and wakes forgetting his own daughter. We see the palace through the king's fraying mind. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined—the monster is also a victim.

chapters.title: Terms of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The guild convenes: helping the child means breaking the law of invisibility that has kept them alive for centuries. Sefa argues for sending the child away; Jonah refuses. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against conscience within a found family.

chapters.title: The Sorcerer's Account
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah infiltrates the court archives disguised as a tax assessor and meets Master Corvane, the court sorcerer—who recognizes the guild instantly and offers a deal: the ledgers for the child's life. Emotional beat: seductive menace; corruption dressed as reasonableness.

chapters.title: Winter Takes the Harbor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The long winter begins early and unnaturally; the city blames the guild's 'witch-work.' The child's power surges, freezing the harbor, and Sefa sacrifices her remaining years to hold it back. Emotional beat: grief, guilt, and the cost of every mercy.

chapters.title: An Oath Written in Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cornered by Corvane's ultimatum, Jonah burns the guild's protective seals and swears a new oath before the founding ledger: truth over safety. The guild hall answers, waking old magic. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Unbinding of Aldric Vey
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Jonah and Aldric POV. In the frozen throne room, Jonah reads the original bargain aloud, using the ledgers' authority to dissolve it. Corvane fights with stolen years; the child and king reach for each other across the room. Emotional beat: terrifying, luminous confrontation where words are weapons.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue in spring. The guild stands openly in the city as a school for the impossible; the king, unbound and uncrowned, plants a garden with the child, who now carries both halves of one name. The final ledger's last line is Jonah's own. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
